title: Wren and the Confession
premise: When a drowned man washes up in the harbor wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, insurance investigator Lior Yarrow realizes the killer isn't just taunting the police — he's taunting her, using details only someone with access to her twelve years of case files could know. As she investigates, Lior discovers the victim was connected to an unsolved death from her first year on the job, one she closed too quickly at the request of the town's beloved police chief. The killer is someone who loved the dead girl from that old case and has spent years studying how Lior buried the truth. In the end, Lior must choose between protecting Chief Aldous Vane — the mentor who shaped her career and whom she loves like family — and confessing her own complicity, and she chooses truth, testifying against Vane even as the killer, the girl's brother, surrenders himself knowing justice will finally be done.
about_author: Coral Sandoval is a former claims adjuster from a small coastal town who spent a decade reading other people's misfortunes in triplicate before turning them into fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary people whose meticulous lives come apart at the seams.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Lior Yarrow's POV. A body surfaces in Graywater Harbor dressed in Lior's own missing cardigan and scarf, and Detective Imara Cole summons her to identify garments she can prove were stolen from her closet. Lior's photographic memory catalogs every detail of the scene. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Reviewing her files at home, she realizes the victim, Daniel Moss, once filed a claim connected to the 2013 drowning of Tessa Vane — the case that made Police Chief Aldous Vane a town hero and launched Lior's career. Someone has been through her filing cabinet. Beat: the past pressing in.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Gave Back
chapters.summary: Imara Cole's POV. The autopsy shows Daniel was held underwater for hours before release; his fingertips are ink-stained, like a clerk or archivist. Imara notices Lior noticed things no civilian should. She begins keeping a private file on Lior herself. Beat: wary alliance forming.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A witness claims she saw Daniel alive wearing Lior's clothes days after they vanished — but Lior's memory proves the woman is lying, coached with details lifted verbatim from Lior's own interview notes. The killer has read her files. Beat: violation and vertigo.

chapters.title: Chief Vane's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Aldous Vane's POV. The chief reassures the town at a press conference while privately pressuring Imara to keep Lior away from the 2013 file. His grief for his daughter Tessa reads as devotion, but small slips suggest he remembers more than he admits. Beat: charm curdling into control.

chapters.title: The Claim That Closed Too Fast
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Reconstructing the 2013 insurance claim from memory, Lior finds the timeline she wrote doesn't match the tide tables — a discrepancy she ignored because Vane asked her to. Guilt surfaces: she built her career on a lie she helped alphabetize. Beat: shame breaking through denial.

chapters.title: Letters in Someone Else's Hand
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. Daniel's apartment yields clippings, photographs, and letters about Tessa Vane — he was researching her death obsessively. Among them, pages copied word-for-word from Lior's confidential reports. Imara confronts Lior, who finally admits the files were compromised. Beat: trust tested by revelation.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the town's memorial gala for Tessa, the killer strikes again — a note pinned inside Lior's coat quoting her very first report, dated the night Tessa died. Vane watches her read it, and something in his face is not surprise. Beat: public poise, private terror.

chapters.title: What Lior Remembers
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Lior's POV, 2013. Young Lior interviews witnesses the night Tessa drowned and notices the boat's fuel log contradicts the chief's account. Vane gently persuades her that grief-stricken families need certainty more than accuracy. She files the report as instructed. Beat: the original sin, tenderly committed.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Waited
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. Digging into Daniel Moss's history, Imara learns he was Tessa's childhood friend — and that his sister Ruth drowned trying to save Tessa that same night, a fact erased from every official record. Two girls died in the water; the town mourned only one. Beat: righteous anger igniting.

chapters.title: A Trap Built From Her Own Words
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Realizing the killer communicates only through details from her files, Lior proposes planting a false detail to flush him out. Imara agrees over Vane's objection. They seed a fabricated witness statement. Beat: Lior turning her curse into a weapon.

chapters.title: The Bait Is Taken
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. The false detail surfaces in an anonymous letter to the newspaper within forty-eight hours, narrowing suspects to those with archive access: Vane, the records clerk, and one other name — Daniel's old employer, the municipal archivist who employed both Daniel and, briefly, young Lior. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: Night at the Records Hall
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Staking out the archives, Lior catches someone rifling the 2013 boxes — not the killer, but Vane, removing pages. He begs her to let it go, invoking their twelve years of loyalty. She refuses. He warns her that some truths drown people. Beat: love and duty colliding head-on.

chapters.title: Ruth
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. Imara locates the Moss family's surviving mother, who reveals Ruth's death was ruled accidental without investigation — Vane signed it off the same week as Tessa's. Daniel grew up knowing his sister was a footnote. Beat: grief given its long-delayed dignity.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The municipal archivist is found dead, staged in Lior's stolen raincoat, holding a page from the suppressed report. The killer is accelerating, punishing anyone who touched the cover-up — and framing Lior as accomplice. Imara must officially consider her a suspect. Beat: betrayal of the badge, isolation deepening.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. Imara questions Lior formally, and Lior lays out everything: the altered 2013 report, Vane's pressure, the archive theft. Her perfect memory makes her either the most credible witness or the most dangerous liar in Graywater. Imara chooses to believe her — quietly, off the record. Beat: fragile faith.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Daniel contacts Lior directly — a phone call she records — demanding she publicly confess her role in burying Ruth's death before he turns himself in. He gives her until the anniversary of the drowning: three days. She hears in his voice a man already finished. Beat: ultimatum and terrible empathy.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Imara POVs. Lior drafts her confession; Vane offers her promotion, protection, silence — everything but accountability. Imara races to find Daniel before the deadline, tracing him to the boathouse where the sisters drowned. Beat: clock ticking, hearts hardening toward truth.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Climax, Lior's POV. On the anniversary night, Lior goes to the boathouse herself and finds Daniel preparing to drown Vane in reenactment. She talks him down not with sympathy but with truth — reciting, flawlessly, his sister's real final hours, proving Ruth died a hero, not a footnote. Vane arrives; Daniel stands down. Beat: mercy won by memory.

chapters.title: What the Chief Buried
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. With Daniel's evidence and Lior's testimony, Vane is arrested for falsifying the 2013 investigations. The town that named a scholarship after him turns overnight. Vane, in cuffs, tells Lior she was always his best student — the cruelest thing he could say. Beat: power unmasked, hollow at last.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On the stand, Lior confesses her own complicity in full, surrendering her license and her reputation, reciting the suppressed facts so precisely that no one can look away. Daniel pleads guilty to manslaughter. Justice arrives imperfect, late, and real. Beat: costly, cleansing honesty.

chapters.title: Alphabetizing the Truth
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Lior's POV. Months later, Lior works as a freelance records auditor helping families reopen cold cases. She visits the harbor where two names now share a memorial stone. She keeps her files still — but the newest folder, labeled honestly, holds her own confession. Beat: quiet peace earned, not granted.
